title: Org Chart: All Direct and Indirect Reports
description:
Given a management hierarchy stored in `employees`, find **all employees who directly or indirectly report to employee id 1 (Ada)** — i.e., the full subtree under Ada. Include Ada herself.

**Table: employees**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| id | INT |
| name | VARCHAR |
| salary | INT |
| manager_id | INT |

Output columns: `id`, `name`, `level` (0 = Ada herself, 1 = direct reports, 2 = their reports, …). Order by `level`, `name`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INT, name VARCHAR, salary INT, manager_id INT); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Ada',200000,NULL),(2,'Ben',150000,1),(3,'Cara',90000,2),(4,'Drew',80000,2),(5,'Eve',120000,1),(6,'Fay',70000,5),(7,'Gil',65000,3);
solution_sql: WITH RECURSIVE org AS (SELECT id, name, 0 AS level FROM employees WHERE id = 1 UNION ALL SELECT e.id, e.name, o.level + 1 FROM employees e JOIN org o ON e.manager_id = o.id) SELECT id, name, level FROM org ORDER BY level, name
hints: A recursive CTE has an anchor (base case) and a recursive part joined by UNION ALL.
Anchor: SELECT the root node. Recursive part: JOIN employees to the CTE on manager_id = cte.id.
explanation: The anchor selects Ada (level 0). Each recursive iteration joins employees whose manager_id matches a node already in the result, adding level+1. Ada→Ben,Eve (level 1)→Cara,Drew,Fay (level 2)→Gil (level 3). Recursion stops when no new rows are added.
